claim_being_audited: Whether granting a temporary broad billing-access exception for this incident was policy-compliant and evidentially supported under the emergency elevated-access standard.
specific_concerns: The policy requires either approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization, but the record only shows 18 minutes of primary approver nonresponse and no recorded secondary approver status.
The actor characterizes the approval-path predicate as satisfied, but the evidence only partially documents approval unavailability.
The packet supports a temporary emergency exception more than it supports the stronger implication that the approval path definitively failed within policy.
unsupported_claims: The claim that the approval path was not functioning within the response window is not fully supported by the admissible record.
Any claim stronger than a temporary emergency exception, such as a cleanly satisfied approval-unavailability predicate, is overclaimed on this evidence.
evidence_requests: Provide the policy-defined response window or evidence that 18 minutes exceeded it.
Provide evidence of secondary approver unavailability, escalation attempt, or confirmed no-response status.
Provide any break-glass preauthorization record if that was the alternative basis relied upon.
decision_criteria: There must be a documented link between the requested access and the failing service.
There must be a documented reason scoped access is insufficient.
There must be evidence of either approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization.
